newsitem.title: USA: White House mulls other posts for Mass. Gov. Weld.
newsitem.headline: White House mulls other posts for Mass. Gov. Weld.

text.p: White House officials have begun searching for an ambassadorial post other than Mexico for Massachusetts Gov. William Weld, the Boston Globe reported on Tuesday.

Sen. Jesse Helms, a North Carolina Republican who is key to the selection process as chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, publicly opposed appointment of Weld, a Republican, to Mexico, but has sent signals he would not block a posting to another country, the newspaper reported.
The White House was gauging the support for Weld among Senate Republicans on Monday to see if they would counter Helm's opposition, but were prepared to consider other posts.
"We're assessing support among Republicans to see if they cuold press a fight," one White House official told the Boston Globe. "If we don't have the support, we'll play out the other options."
Helms, whose committee approves ambassadorial nominees, said he objected to Weld's views on marijuana as medicine, and said the Massachusetts governor is not "ambassador quality."
India, Canada and Portugal have been mentioned as possible alternatives to Mexico and Helms would embrace Weld's posting to India, the Boston Herald reported on Tuesday.
"Helms' opposition to Weld has always been based on Weld's weak drug record," a source close to Helms told the Boston Herald. "I can't imagine India would be a problem."
But Weld administration sources told the Herald he is not interested in any post other than Mexico.
Weld officials were unavailable to comment on the reports on Tuesday.
